text.p: Novartis, the Swiss pharmaceuticals company arising from the merger of Sandoz AG and Ciba-Geigy AG, said on Thursday it would streamline its national health care manufacturing and distribution system in the United States.

Doug Watson, the designated U.S. president and Chief Executive Officer of Novartis, also said the company would cut its national health care manufacturing and distribution work force by about 205 employees, a decrease of less than 10 percent.
The company said it would streamline its U.S. manufacturing and distribution system for branded and generic prescription pharmaceuticals, as well as for over-the-counter products.

"The merger of Ciba and Sandoz results in a duplication in resources and provides an opportunity for Novartis to consolidate health care manufacturing and distribution facilities into a more streamlined, cost effective system," Watson said.

To consolidate, some Ciba and Sandoz health care manufacturing and distribution sites would be closed over the next five years, the company said. These included the Summit, N.J. and Fort Washington, Pa. sites, it said.
